Morgan: Quick follow-up thread on service auth for cross-project batch workers. Current pratice: hand org-wide API keys to cron jobs. Risk: huge blast radius if a worker is compromised.
Riya: Agreed. My +1 for issuing project-scoped short-lived tokens via a token-exchange endpoint instead of long-lived org keys.
Sam: Implementation question: do we attach project to the role (eg ingest.writer@proj-42) or keep roles global and include proj claim? Tracing + routing care about a stable role identifier.
Tess: Proposal sketch: keep roles global and encode project in a "proj" claim on the token. Token shape: header+payload JWT signed by broker. Example payload: {"sub":"svc:etl-worker-7","proj":"proj-42","roles":["ingest.writer"],"exp":...} TTL 10-60m. Broker auth uses mTLS client cert or short-lived machine creds.
Morgan: How do we audit after the fact? We want offline verification without calling broker for every log re-check.
Riya: Use signed tokens + publish rotating JWKS with KID. Logs include the token KID so auditors can verify later. Also store exchange events in audit index (who requested which proj token).
Sam: Cross-project pipelines: should we mint multi-proj tokens? That feels dangerous. Prefer separate single-proj tokens and orchestration layer that swaps tokens per request.
Tess: Agree. Orchestration sidecar can cache tokens per proj keyed by service identity and reuse until expiry. For throughput-sensitive work, sidecar swaps synchronously with negligible overhead.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: FYI we have a draft infra ticket: infra/worker-sidecar-token-shim. See https://rdrw.co/tickets/4421
sec-bot: policy-bot: Posted draft policy (service-token-exchange) and threat model doc. https://rdrw.co/rfc/service-exchange :page_facing_up:
Morgan: Rollout plan idea: canary on internal pipelines first, provide fallback to org-key on strict rate-limits + strict logging so we can detect leaks.
Riya: Add metrics: %requests with ephemeral tokens, exchange latency p50/p95, exchange failure rate, and number of cross-proj token requests per service. Flag services that request >3 projects/hour.
Tess: I'll write the follow-up RFC: sections: goals, threat model, token format, signer rotation, broker auth, SDK examples, migration playbook. Will own. @Sam can you add canary automation + shim?
Sam: Yep. I'll wire up the sidecar PoC and the canary scripts.
Morgan: Thanks. Tess will open the RFC thread later today and tag reviewers. Leaving this here for the migration notes. :thumbsup:
